paper_metadata.title: Quantum Machine Learning: An Application of Quantum Support Vector Machines for Financial Data Classification

experiments.description: Quantum Support Vector Machine (QSVM) financial data classification using a Cirq-based quantum kernel on a small binary synthetic dataset, compared against classical SVM as a baseline.

algorithm.variant: Quantum kernel SVM implemented with Google Cirq

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical binary feature vectors x are encoded into a 2-qubit circuit using Hadamard gates on both qubits, followed by conditional CNOT operations when x[i] == 1.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary classification via SVM with quantum kernel K(x,y)=|<phi(x)|phi(y)>|^2

problem_instance.description: Binary classification on a randomly generated 2-feature dataset used as a toy financial-data classification demonstration.

dataset_specification.description: X = np.random.randint(0, 2, size=(100, 2)); y = np.random.randint(0, 2, size=100); train_test_split used with test_size reported in code snippet but truncated in text.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: No domain-specific preprocessing reported; synthetic binary data generated directly.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Single train/test evaluation; reported test accuracy for QSVM and classical SVM.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Synthetic binary data generation; pairwise quantum kernel matrix construction for training and test sets.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: SVM prediction on precomputed kernel matrices; accuracy computed with sklearn.metrics.accuracy_score.

speedup_claims.conditions: on the toy synthetic dataset used in the paper; QSVM claimed to take a few seconds while classical SVM took several minutes
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper does not provide exact timing measurements, hardware details, or repeated-run statistics; the speedup is based on a qualitative comparison in text.

speedup_claims.conditions: as claimed in the discussion of quantum feature mapping and Hilbert-space representation
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a general claim about quantum feature spaces and not a measured result from the experiment.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Not specified; paper claims exponential scaling with number of qubits for the feature space representation.
complexity_analysis.wall_clock_quantum: few seconds (claimed for QSVM training in text)
complexity_analysis.wall_clock_classical: several minutes (claimed for classical SVM training in text)
